description.narrative:
IFES vision is "Democracy for a better future" that is to be realized through their stated mission: "Together we build democracies that deliver for all".
In response to emerging threats and opportunities, IFES has identified four distinct and mutually reinforcing strategic outcomes:
Strategic Outcome 1: Trusted electoral institutions deliver credible elections Strategic Objectives: 1.1 Support transparent, safe and inclusive electoral processes that lead to accepted outcomes 1.2 Build the capacity of electoral institutions to deliver credible elections over time 1.3 Enable electoral officials to pro-actively address emerging challenges and sustain public trust in elections
Strategic Outcome 2: Effective governing institutions accountable to the people they serve Strategic Objectives: 2.1 Strengthen the efforts of public officials and civil society to promote good governance and the rule of law and counter corruption 2.2 Assist local partners to design durable democratic systems and institutions that enable successful and stable transitions 2.3 Galvanize champions of democratic reform in closing spaces
Strategic Outcome 3: All people safely participate in civic and political life on an equal basis Strategic Objectives: 3.1 Support civil society, academia and government partners to make a sustained commitment to civic education, robust youth engagement and conflict mitigation 3.2 Advance gender equality and womens rights, empowerment and leadership in political and public life by breaking down individual and structural obstacles 3.3 Empower Black, Indigenous and people of color; people with disabilities; displaced persons; and other marginalized groups to exercise political rights and be recognized as critical constituencies 3.4 Support civil society in established democracies as well as transitional and closing spaces to respond to challenges facing democracy and human rights
Strategic Outcome 4: Technology, information and data positively serve elections and democracy Strategic Objectives: 4.1 Strengthen digital security and ensure the responsible and transparent use of election technologies 4.2 Promote the responsible use of technology and new and traditional media platforms to enable informed and positive political discourse and engagement
Cross-cutting Approach: Design and implement impactful programs based on research, evidence and comparative international standards and experience
Institutional Capacities and Outcomes
IFES also has three institutional outcomes to develop IFES capacities and efficiencies and better position the organization to advance its vision and mission:
Institutional Outcome 1: Talent management that meets the needs of the organization and the people Institutional Objectives: 1.1 Develop recruiting strategy; identify and fill current expertise gaps 1.2 Institutionalize programmatic learning 1.3 Operationalize proactive recruiting strategy 1.4 Introduce learning and development program 1.5 Develop performance, rewards and recognition
Institutional Outcome 2: Ability to constructively influence policy and practice in the DRG sector Institutional Objectives: 2.1 Establish development and strategic communications unit and prepare new business development and communications strategy 2.2 Strengthen strategic communications and HQ/field communications 2.3 Fully operationalize new strategy
Institutional Outcome 3: Calibrated alignment and orientation of all parts of the organization toward excellence Institutional Objectives: 3.1 Identify financial management system improvements and areas of current system/process improvement potential 3.2 Implement financial management system improvements 3.3 Operationalize improvements in critical HR systems

International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES) ges ett kärnstöd på 10 000 000 kr/år under tre år, 2021-2024, för genomförandet av sin strategiska plan 2020-2024. För närvarande är en mycket liten del av IFES finansiering kärnstöd. Ett kärnstöd från Sida skulle göra det möjligt för IFES att avsevärt öka sin förmåga och flexibilitet att utveckla nya metoder, lära, producera och dela kunskap, särskilt inriktat på de mest sårbara och utsatta. Det mesta av detta arbete kommer att ske vid huvudkontoret i Arlington, USA, men skulle gynna ett stort antal ODA-berättigade länder, givet IFES globala täckning. Den strategiska planen kommer kontinuerligt att ses över och revideras under dess genomförande.

International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES) receives financial support of 10 000 000 SEK/year for three years, 2021-2024 for core support for realization of its Strategic Plan 2020-2024. Currently a very small part of IFES' funding is core support. A possible core support from Sida would enable IFES to significantly step up its ability to innovate, pilot new methods, learn, produce and share knowledge, especially targeting the most disadvantaged and vulnerable people. Most of this work will take place at headquarters in Arlington, USA, but would benefit a large range of ODA eligible countries, seeing IFES global footprint. The strategic plan will be continually reviewed and revised during its implementation.

description.narrative:
Selected results from IFES Annual Narrative report for March 2025- January 2026:
* An updated methodology to assess the readiness of electoral institutions to administer major electoral events and a detailed white paper on out-of-country voting (OCV) that includes key new considerations, including the integration of AI into OCV systems.
* Products and innovations developed with Sida support have been used in more than 45 business development initiatives, including at least 10 that already have led to funded projects (e.g., EMB readiness assessment in Bangladesh, civic edutainment tools in Papua New Guinea, and approaches to fostering a democratic culture in Syria).
* Since USAID was dismantled, IFES also has taken on a leading role in ensuring the sustainability of the Global Network for Securing Electoral Integrity (GNSEI) by performing secretariat functions for the network, including revising Network workplans, organizing full Network meetings, coordinating outreach to Network participants and observers to confirm their continued interest and capacity to contribute to GNSEI activities moving forward, and planning and implementing elections for a new term for the Steering Committee. The newly installed Steering Committee has made progress in developing a workplan for the year and distributing responsibilities across its members for enhanced sustainability.
* During this award period, IFES completed a comprehensive update and expansion of a previously published white paper on out-of-country voting (OCV). The paper leverages desk research and in-house expertise as well as consultations with electoral management bodies (EMBs) and external peer reviewers. The white paper was employed to guide IFES support to the Moldovan EMB during the September 2025 elections, as authorities expanded OCV postal voting to 10 countries following a successful 2024 pilot Furthermore, IFES advised the Bangladesh Election Commission (BEC) as they identified an OCV solution to enable the expansion of the franchise to Bangladeshs significant diaspora community across the world for the February 2026 transitional elections. Technical assistance offered to these EMBs included analysis of the OCV options and their associated risks and supported EMB engagements with other national stakeholders to coordinate an effective and inclusive OCV planning process. In Dhaka, IFES presented the OCV considerations at a conference organized by the BEC that engaged state agencies, civil society representatives, academics, technology vendors, and political parties.
* At the request of the BEC and the election donor group in Dhaka, IFES SO1 team deployed to Bangladesh to undertake an assessment of the BECs readiness to deliver timely and credible elections. This proved to be an ideal opportunity to pilot IFES EMB Readiness Assessment Methodology cofunded by Sida. The findings were shared with the BEC and informed its adjustments to voter education approaches, poll worker training, stakeholder engagement, and internal communications.
* IFES steered civil society inputs and coordination and led strong advocacy for the first-ever UnitedNations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC) resolution on political finance, which attracted nearly 60 country co-sponsors and was unanimously adopted at the December 2025 UNCAC Conference of States Parties (CoSP) in Doha, Qatar. The resolution, "Preventing and combating corruption through enhancing transparency in the funding of political parties, candidatures for elected public obice, and electoral campaigns outlines the most detailed global standards on political finance ever available. IFES active role in the advocacy for this resolution began in late 2022 and continued until the moment of adoption. IFES posted about the resolution online and co-drafted the open letter on political finance integrity, which was endorsed by 148 organizations around the world.
* With Sida core funding support in 2025, IFES completed an update to the Violence Against Women in Elections Framework (VAWE), originally published in 2016. The new framework consolidates key lessons learned from a decades worth of IFES assessments in the field, provides new guidance and information on the role of Technology-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence (TFGBV), includes information on the specific challenges facing women from the LGBTQI community, and launches a streamlined approach to documenting violence against women. The new framework also includes specific guidance and recommendations for EMBs to use in preventing and mitigating VAWE.
* IFES shared comparative international experience and advocated for disability rights in the electionspace at country-specific events such as The Future of Inclusive Elections in Barbados and MakingUgandan Elections Inclusive for All. Global advocacy included: UN Special Rapporteur report on the rights of persons with disabilities: IFES submitted written feedback to a call for submissions on the political representation of persons with disabilities and their right to hold public office. As a result of IFES submission, the Special Rapporteur office conducted a follow-up interview with IFES to discuss the topic in more detail.
